q18726.en: A driver, besides following the specific traffic rules, must behave correctly and tolerantly towards other road users.

explain.short: Driving is not only about rules: you share the road, so respect and tolerance towards others are part of your duty.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'oltre a' means 'besides': rules AND good behaviour are both required.

sceneParams.caption: Rules plus respect for other road users
lines: Be correct and tolerant with others

q18727.en: When approaching a junction, a driver must always use maximum care, even when the other drivers must give way to him.

explain.short: Having priority does not make you safe: the others may not stop, so you approach every junction with maximum care.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'anche quando' (even when) is the key: care is needed even with priority.

sceneParams.caption: Priority, but still maximum care at junctions

q18728.en: The driver of a vehicle must protect his own safety and that of others.

explain.short: Every driver is responsible for safety: his own and that of everyone around him.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'la propria e l'altrui' means 'his own AND others'': both, not only one.

sceneParams.caption: Protect your safety and everyone else's

q18729.en: The driver of a vehicle must respect traffic officers and cooperate with them.

explain.short: Traffic officers (agenti del traffico) keep the road safe, so drivers must respect them and follow their directions.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'collaborare' means 'cooperate': not just tolerate them, but help them.

sceneParams.caption: Respect and cooperate with traffic police

q18730.en: The driver of a vehicle must try to predict the behaviour of other road users.

explain.short: Thinking ahead about what others might do gives you time to react before a danger happens.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'prevedere' means 'predict, foresee': a key skill of defensive driving.

sceneParams.caption: Think ahead: what will the others do?

q18731.en: The driver of a vehicle must be patient and tolerant even when traffic slows down.

explain.short: Slow traffic happens to everyone: getting nervous leads to risky moves, so stay patient.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'anche in caso di' means 'even in case of': patience also in jams.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic slows down: stay calm and patient

q18732.en: The driver of a vehicle must not always rely on the behaviour of others, which may not be correct.

explain.short: Other people make mistakes. If you always trust them, their mistake becomes your crash.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'non deve fare sempre affidamento' = 'must not always rely': trust, but check.

sceneParams.caption: Others can make mistakes: don't trust blindly

q18733.en: The driver of a vehicle cannot insist on going first when there is a doubt that he will not be given priority.

explain.short: If you are not sure the other driver will let you pass, forcing your way is dangerous: wait and be sure.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'quando sorge il dubbio' = 'when there is a doubt': in doubt, do not force.

sceneParams.caption: In doubt? Don't force your priority

q18734.en: The right of way does not allow the driver to cross the junction without using care.

explain.short: Priority (precedenza) tells who should go first, but you must still look and be careful.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'non autorizza' = 'does not allow': priority is not a licence to be careless.

sceneParams.caption: Right of way still needs care
lines: You have the right of way

q18735.en: The driver of a large vehicle, as a rule, has priority over the driver of a smaller vehicle.

explain.short: Priority depends on signs and road rules, not on how big a vehicle is.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) makes it sound official, but size never gives priority.

sceneParams.caption: Size does NOT give priority

q18736.en: The driver of a vehicle may take advantage of his vehicle's power so as not to give way to those who have priority.

explain.short: A powerful engine gives no rights: you must give way to whoever has priority.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'può approfittare' (may take advantage) is the false part: power is not a right.

sceneParams.caption: Power is no excuse: give way when due

q18737.en: The driver of a heavy vehicle may behave in a way that annoys other road users.

explain.short: Every driver, heavy vehicle or not, must be correct and tolerant towards others.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'può' (may) is the trap: annoying others is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy vehicles must respect others too

q18738.en: The driver of a vehicle must respect traffic officers only if they are in uniform.

explain.short: Traffic officers must always be respected; the rule does not depend on wearing a uniform.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) adds a false limit.

sceneParams.caption: Respect officers always, not only in uniform

q18739.en: The driver of a vehicle may do without maximum care when approaching a junction where he has the right of way.

explain.short: Even with the right of way, you must approach a junction with maximum care: others may not stop.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'può fare a meno' (may do without) is the false part.

sceneParams.caption: Even with priority, keep maximum care
lines: You have priority at the junction

q18740.en: The driver must show signs of impatience if the vehicle in front is going too slowly.

explain.short: Showing impatience (horn, flashing, tailgating) only creates danger: stay calm and keep your distance.
explain.rule: A good driver is patient, careful and respectful: protect everyone's safety, respect traffic police and never rely blindly on others.
explain.trap: 'deve' (must) makes it absurd: impatience is never a duty.

sceneParams.caption: Slow car ahead: stay calm, keep distance

q18741.en: A crash, even at low speed, could cause serious physical harm to pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists, if involved.

explain.short: Pedestrians and riders have no bodywork to protect them, so even a slow crash can hurt them badly.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'anche a bassa velocità' = 'even at low speed': slow does not mean harmless.

sceneParams.caption: Even a slow crash can badly hurt riders
lines: Even a slow crash is serious

q18742.en: You must frequently check in the rear-view mirror whether a cyclist or motorcyclist is coming.

explain.short: Bikes and motorbikes are small and fast to appear, so you check your mirrors often.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'frequentemente' (frequently): not once, but often.

sceneParams.caption: Check mirrors often for bikes and motorbikes

q18743.en: After parking the vehicle at the side of the carriageway, before opening the door the driver must check that no cyclists or motorcyclists are coming.

explain.short: A door opened suddenly can hit a passing cyclist or motorcyclist, so look first.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'prima di aprire lo sportello' = 'before opening the door': the check comes first.

sceneParams.caption: Look behind before opening the door

q18744.en: The internal pillars of motor vehicles affect visibility.

explain.short: The pillars (montanti) that hold up the roof block part of your view and create blind spots.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'montanti' are the roof pillars of the car, not the mirrors.

sceneParams.caption: Car pillars create blind spots
lines: They hide part of the view

q18745.en: The internal pillars of motor vehicles reduce the chance of seeing a cyclist or a motorcyclist.

explain.short: A slim bike or motorbike can hide completely behind a pillar, so move your head to check.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'riducono' (reduce): pillars really hide small road users.

sceneParams.caption: A cyclist can hide behind a pillar

q18746.en: A low-speed crash does not cause safety problems for the drivers involved.

explain.short: Even a slow crash can injure people, especially riders and pedestrians.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'non crea problemi' is the false claim: low speed is not harmless.

sceneParams.caption: Low speed crashes can still injure

q18747.en: A driver getting out of a parked vehicle does not have to check whether cyclists are coming.

explain.short: Before opening the door you must always check for cyclists, or you could knock them down.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'non deve controllare' (does not have to check) is the false part.

sceneParams.caption: You MUST check for cyclists before getting out

q18748.en: In the rear-view mirror the driver must only check whether lorries or buses are coming.

explain.short: The mirror is for everyone behind you, especially small and fast bikes and motorbikes.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: you check for every road user.

sceneParams.caption: Mirrors: check for ALL users, not only trucks

q18749.en: A motorcycle rider may zigzag between vehicles stopped at a traffic light.

explain.short: Weaving between stopped cars is dangerous: drivers do not expect you and doors may open.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'può fare lo slalom' (may zigzag) is the false permission.

sceneParams.caption: No zigzagging between stopped cars

q18750.en: A motorcycle rider may park on the pavement even if there are no dedicated parking spaces.

explain.short: The pavement (marciapiede) is for pedestrians: a motorbike may park there only in marked spaces.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'anche se non vi sono' (even if there are none) is the false part.

sceneParams.caption: No parking on the pavement without marked spaces

q18751.en: A motorcycle rider may ride on the pavement if traffic on the carriageway is blocked.

explain.short: Vehicles may never ride on the pavement: it belongs to pedestrians, whatever the traffic.
explain.rule: Pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists have no protection: check mirrors often, look before opening the door, and remember the car pillars hide them.
explain.trap: 'se il traffico è bloccato' sounds like an excuse, but there is none.

sceneParams.caption: Never ride on the pavement, even in a jam

q18752.en: You must use greater care towards disabled people.

explain.short: Disabled people may move slowly or with difficulty, so you need more care.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'diversamente abili' means 'disabled people'.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with disabled people

q18753.en: You must use greater care towards elderly people.

explain.short: Elderly people may see, hear and react more slowly, so you need more care.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'anziane' means 'elderly'.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with elderly people

q18754.en: You must use greater care towards children crossing the road.

explain.short: Children are small, hard to see and unpredictable, so you need more care.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'bambini' means 'children': always a group needing care.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with children crossing

q18755.en: You must use greater care towards drivers who show uncertain driving.

explain.short: A driver who seems unsure may make sudden mistakes, so keep your distance and be careful.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'guida incerta' means 'uncertain, hesitant driving'.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with uncertain drivers

q18756.en: You must use greater care towards drivers of vehicles adapted for disabled people.

explain.short: These drivers may have reduced movement, so give them more space and patience.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'veicoli adattati' means 'adapted vehicles' for disabled drivers.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with adapted vehicles
lines: drivers of vehicles adapted for disabled people

q18757.en: You must use greater care towards people on bicycles and those with limited mobility.

explain.short: Cyclists are unprotected and people with limited mobility are slow, so you need more care.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'scarsa capacità di movimento' means 'limited ability to move'.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with cyclists and slow walkers
lines: cyclists and people who move with difficulty

q18758.en: You must use particular care towards drivers who got their driving licence in a foreign country.

explain.short: A foreign licence says nothing about how well someone drives; it is not a special category.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'Stato estero' (foreign country) sounds like a reason, but it is not.

sceneParams.caption: A foreign licence is no reason for special care
lines: No special reason for extra care
a foreign licence is no special reason

q18759.en: You must use greater care towards drivers of electric motor vehicles.

explain.short: Electric cars are driven like any other car: the type of engine is not a reason for extra care.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'elettrici' (electric) is the distractor: the engine type does not matter.

sceneParams.caption: Electric cars need no special care
lines: No special reason for extra care
electric cars are no special reason

q18760.en: You must use greater care towards taxi drivers.

explain.short: Taxi drivers are normal drivers, not a vulnerable group.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'taxi' is the distractor: the job is not a risk category.

sceneParams.caption: Taxi drivers need no special care
lines: No special reason for extra care
taxi drivers are no special reason

q18761.en: You must use greater care towards drivers of motor tricycles.

explain.short: Motor tricycles are ordinary motor vehicles; the rule lists weak road users, not vehicle types.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'tricicli a motore' (motor tricycles) is the distractor.

sceneParams.caption: Motor tricycles need no special care
lines: No special reason for extra care
motor tricycles are no special reason

q18762.en: You must use greater care towards pedestrians with a white stick, but not those with a white-and-red stick.

explain.short: A white stick means blind, a white-and-red stick means deaf-blind: both need great care.
explain.rule: Take extra care with weak or unpredictable road users: children, elderly and disabled people, cyclists and uncertain drivers.
explain.trap: 'ma non' (but not) wrongly excludes the white-red stick.

sceneParams.caption: White-red stick (deaf-blind) needs care too

q18763.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that they may not pay enough attention to vehicles.

explain.short: Elderly people may be distracted or not notice your car, so you must be the careful one.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'potrebbero' (they might): you must expect it.

sceneParams.caption: They may not notice your car

q18764.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that they may stop suddenly in the middle of the road.

explain.short: An elderly person may hesitate and stop halfway, so be ready to stop.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'improvvisamente' (suddenly): expect sudden stops.

sceneParams.caption: They may stop in the middle of the road

keywords.en: in the middle of the road

q18765.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that they may look neither right nor left.

explain.short: Some elderly people cross without looking, so you must watch for them.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'né... né' means 'neither... nor'.

sceneParams.caption: They may cross without looking

q18766.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that, because of their age, they do not react quickly to danger.

explain.short: With age, reactions get slower, so they may not jump out of the way in time.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'non reagiscono prontamente' = 'do not react quickly'.

sceneParams.caption: Slow reactions to danger

q18767.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, do not get too close with the vehicle, so they do not feel threatened and react with dangerous movements.

explain.short: A car too close can frighten them into a sudden, risky movement: keep your distance.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'non bisogna avvicinarsi troppo' = 'do not get too close'.

sceneParams.caption: Keep your distance, don't scare them

q18768.en: Elderly people crossing the carriageway face greater dangers, because their sight and hearing are no longer excellent.

explain.short: Weaker eyes and ears mean they may not see or hear your car coming.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'visive e uditive' = 'of sight and hearing'.

sceneParams.caption: Weaker sight and hearing

q18769.en: Elderly people crossing the carriageway face greater dangers, because they may misjudge the speed of approaching vehicles.

explain.short: They may think a car is slower or farther than it is and start to cross.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'valutare male' = 'misjudge'.

sceneParams.caption: They may misjudge your speed

q18770.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that they have quicker reflexes and therefore cross more carefully.

explain.short: It is the opposite: with age, reflexes become slower, not quicker.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'più rapidi' (quicker) is the false word.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: their reflexes are slower

q18771.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that they usually cross quickly and carefully.

explain.short: Elderly people usually cross slowly and with difficulty, not quickly.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'rapidamente' (quickly) is the false word.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: they usually cross slowly

q18772.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, keep in mind that, having more experience and a wider field of vision, they sense danger better.

explain.short: With age the field of vision gets narrower, and they notice danger later, not sooner.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'campo visivo maggiore' (wider vision) is false.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: their vision is weaker

q18773.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must flash your lights and sound the horn to make them cross quickly.

explain.short: Flashing and honking can frighten them and cause a fall or a sudden stop: wait calmly.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'bisogna lampeggiare' (you must flash) is false.

sceneParams.caption: Never flash or honk at them: wait

q18774.en: When elderly people cross the carriageway, you must give way only to those crossing from left to right.

explain.short: You give way to every pedestrian crossing, whatever the direction.
explain.rule: Elderly pedestrians see, hear and react more slowly: expect them to stop or hesitate, keep your distance and let them cross calmly.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) adds a false limit about the direction.

sceneParams.caption: Give way to all, from any side

q18775.en: The driver must stop and give way to a blind pedestrian with a white stick who is about to cross the road outside the zebra crossing.

explain.short: A blind person cannot see you, so you stop for them wherever they cross.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'fuori dalle strisce' (outside the crossing) does not cancel the duty.

sceneParams.caption: Stop for a white stick, even off the crossing

q18776.en: The driver must stop and make it easier for a blind pedestrian with a white stick to cross the road outside the zebra crossing.

explain.short: You stop and let the blind person cross calmly, helping them as much as you can.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'facilitare' means 'make easier, help'.

sceneParams.caption: Stop and help them cross

q18777.en: The driver must give way to a blind pedestrian with a white stick crossing the road outside the zebra crossing, even if not accompanied by a guide dog.

explain.short: The white stick alone is enough: a guide dog is not required for priority.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'anche se non' (even if not): no dog needed.

sceneParams.caption: White stick is enough, no dog needed
lines: Give way, dog or no dog

q18778.en: The driver must stop to give way to a deaf-blind pedestrian who, with a white-and-red stick, crosses the road outside the zebra crossing.

explain.short: A white-and-red stick means deaf-blind: they can neither see nor hear you, so you stop.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'sordocieco' means 'deaf-blind'.

sceneParams.caption: White-red stick: deaf-blind, stop

q18779.en: The driver must give way to a pedestrian with a white or white-and-red stick crossing the road, even outside the stripes of a pedestrian crossing.

explain.short: Both sticks give priority, wherever the person crosses.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'anche se è fuori' (even if outside): place does not matter.

sceneParams.caption: Both sticks: priority everywhere
lines: Give way, on or off the crossing

q18780.en: The driver must stop when a blind pedestrian with a white stick is about to cross the road, avoiding sudden braking so as not to frighten them.

explain.short: A blind person relies on hearing: screeching brakes can frighten them, so stop smoothly.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'bruscamente' means 'sharply, suddenly'.

sceneParams.caption: Stop smoothly, don't scare them

q18781.en: The driver must accelerate to clear the carriageway quickly when a blind pedestrian with a white stick crosses the road without a guide dog.

explain.short: You must stop and give way, never speed up near a blind pedestrian.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'accelerare' (accelerate) is the false word.

sceneParams.caption: Never accelerate: stop and give way

q18782.en: The driver must go first, since he has priority, when a blind pedestrian with a white stick crosses the road outside the zebra crossing.

explain.short: The blind pedestrian has priority, not the driver, even outside the zebra crossing.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'ha la precedenza' is false: the priority belongs to the pedestrian.

sceneParams.caption: Priority is the blind pedestrian's
lines: The driver does NOT go first

q18783.en: When a blind pedestrian with a white stick crosses outside the zebra crossing, the driver must give way only if the pedestrian crossing is more than 100 metres away.

explain.short: There is no distance condition: a blind pedestrian always gets priority.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'solo se... oltre 100 metri' invents a limit.

sceneParams.caption: No 100 m rule: always give way

q18784.en: The driver must give way to a blind pedestrian crossing outside the zebra crossing only if they have a white-and-red stick.

explain.short: Both the white stick and the white-and-red stick give priority.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) wrongly excludes the plain white stick.

sceneParams.caption: White stick counts too, not only white-red

q18785.en: The driver must expect that a blind pedestrian with a white stick crossing outside the zebra crossing will walk quickly and without hesitation.

explain.short: A blind person usually moves slowly and carefully, feeling the way with the stick.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'rapidamente e senza incertezza' is the false part.

sceneParams.caption: Expect slow, careful steps

q18786.en: If a pedestrian with a white stick crosses the road outside the zebra crossing, you must sound the horn to urge them to cross quickly.

explain.short: The horn would frighten a blind person: stop quietly and wait.
explain.rule: A pedestrian with a white stick (blind) or a white-and-red stick (deaf-blind) always has priority, even outside the zebra crossing: stop gently and help them cross.
explain.trap: 'suonare il clacson' (sound the horn) is the false action.

sceneParams.caption: Never honk: stop quietly

q18787.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that a pedestrian, while crossing, may become unsure and suddenly turn back.

explain.short: Pedestrians can change their mind halfway, so be ready to stop.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'ritornare improvvisamente indietro' = 'suddenly turn back'.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian may suddenly turn back

q18788.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that elderly people usually cross slowly and with difficulty.

explain.short: Elderly people need more time to cross, so be patient.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'solitamente' means 'usually'.

sceneParams.caption: Elderly people cross slowly

q18789.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that children's reactions while crossing are unpredictable and can therefore create danger.

explain.short: Children can run, stop or change direction at any moment.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'imprevedibili' means 'unpredictable'.

sceneParams.caption: Children are unpredictable

q18790.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that children may step onto the stripes and then suddenly go back, for no apparent reason.

explain.short: Children may start crossing and run back without any reason: be ready.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'senza motivo apparente' = 'for no apparent reason'.

sceneParams.caption: Children may go back without reason

q18791.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that a pedestrian may stop suddenly on the stripes of the crossing.

explain.short: A pedestrian may stop halfway, so you must be able to stop too.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'improvvisamente' (suddenly): expect it.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian may stop on the stripes

q18792.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that pedestrians, especially children, can suddenly appear from between parked vehicles.

explain.short: Parked cars hide people; children especially can pop out from between them.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'sbucare' means 'pop out, appear suddenly'.

sceneParams.caption: Children can pop out between parked cars

q18793.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that vehicles parked close to the stripes block the view of pedestrians.

explain.short: Cars parked near the crossing hide pedestrians from you and you from them.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'impediscono la visuale' = 'block the view'.

sceneParams.caption: Parked cars hide pedestrians

q18794.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must expect children to react quickly and behave correctly.

explain.short: Children are unpredictable: never expect correct behaviour from them.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'comportamento corretto' is the false expectation.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: children are unpredictable

q18795.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, pedestrians must wave their hand before starting to cross.

explain.short: No rule requires pedestrians to signal: you must watch for them anyway.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'devono fare un cenno' invents a duty.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: pedestrians need not wave

keywords.it: fare un cenno con la mano

q18796.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that a pedestrian with a white stick has more experience in crossing the carriageway.

explain.short: A white stick means a blind person: they are more at risk, so you need more care.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'più esperienza' (more experience) is the false idea.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: a blind pedestrian is more at risk

q18797.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must stop if the crossing pedestrian has a white-and-red stick; he only has to slow down if they have a white stick.

explain.short: You must stop for both: white stick and white-and-red stick.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'deve solo rallentare' (only slow down) is the false part.

sceneParams.caption: Stop for white AND white-red sticks

q18798.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must accelerate just enough to pass in front of the crossing pedestrian.

explain.short: The pedestrian on the crossing has priority: you slow down and stop.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'accelerare' (accelerate) is the false action.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: slow down and stop

q18799.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that if the pedestrian has stopped in the middle of the stripes, it means he has given up his right to cross.

explain.short: A pedestrian who stops is still crossing: wait until they finish.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'ha rinunciato' (gave up) is the false idea.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: they still have priority

keywords.en: in the middle of the stripes

q18800.en: Near a pedestrian crossing, the driver must consider that pedestrians must cross the road side by side, so as to take less time.

explain.short: No such rule exists: pedestrians may cross as they need to.
explain.rule: Near a zebra crossing expect pedestrians to hesitate, stop or turn back, and children to appear suddenly: slow down and be ready to stop.
explain.trap: 'devono... affiancati' invents a duty.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: no 'side by side' rule
